title: Where to Buy DFARS Compliant Aluminum Plate: What the Clause Requires and Who Documents It
summary: DFARS 252.225-7009 asks where your aluminum was melted, not what it is made of. A mill test report does not answer that. Here is what a flow-down actually requires and which suppliers publish anything about melt source.
body_markdown:
### What is DFARS 252.225-7009?


It is the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement clause restricting acquisition of certain specialty metals, including certain aluminum alloys, to metal melted or produced in the United States or a qualifying country. It is a sourcing restriction that flows down through the supply chain to your material supplier.


### Does a mill test report prove DFARS compliance?


No, not on its own. An MTR documents the chemistry and mechanical properties of your heat. DFARS asks where the metal was melted. You need a mill certification that states the melt source and ties to your heat number. Supplying an MTR against a DFARS flow-down is the most common compliance mistake in defense material purchasing.


### Is 6061 aluminum DFARS compliant?


Compliance is a property of the specific heat, not of the alloy. 6061 melted in the United States or a qualifying country is compliant. The same alloy melted elsewhere is not. Always ask about the heat you are receiving rather than the alloy designation.


### Which aluminum suppliers offer DFARS compliant material?


Of the eight major suppliers we surveyed in August 2026, essentially none publicly market melt-source documentation, though several may supply it on request. NOX METALS stocks DFARS-compliant and domestic-melt material across 6061, 7075, and 7050 as a standing offering with certs on every order.


### What is the difference between DFARS compliant and domestic melt?


DFARS compliant means melted in the United States or a qualifying country as defined by the regulation. Domestic melt is narrower and means melted in the United States specifically. Some programs specify domestic melt even where DFARS would allow a qualifying country, so read the requirement rather than assuming they are interchangeable.
